title: Compare palettes across the nine themes
---

Choose the chart configuration that matches your blog or slides, then download or
reproduce it in your plotting language. Compare the Folio, Nocturne and Tufte specimens
below. They use the same data and scientific palettes, while their fonts, backgrounds,
axes, labels and ink edges match each theme.

 Read the top row as a comparison of named categories. It shows categorical lines and an
explicit five-slot marker option. The recommended variant has three slots. The bottom
row uses sequential cividis for magnitude and diverging BrBG for change around a
meaningful center.

A crossed heatmap cell means missing. An uncrossed cell at the diverging center means a
measured center value. Changing theme or dark mode never reverses or recolors the
scientific maps to match a brand accent.

## Compare your blog or slide configuration

Choose the same **Family**, **Mode**, **Profile** and **Surface** as your target
document, then choose your plotting interface. Start with
[Folio for a light reading page](plotting-gallery.qmd?theme=folio&mode=light&profile=reading&surface=paper),
[Nocturne for a dark presentation panel](plotting-gallery.qmd?theme=nocturne&mode=dark&profile=presentation&surface=panel),
or [Tufte for a light reading page](plotting-gallery.qmd?theme=tufte&mode=light&profile=reading&surface=paper).
Use **intended** preview size before judging label readability.

The selector covers 72 configurations and 216 interface views. It combines nine
families, two modes, two profiles and two surfaces with Python/Matplotlib,
R/ggplot2 and base R. The website displays reviewed static exports without
running a plotting engine. JavaScript uses the same scientific contract and has
its [own interactive example and native configuration recipe](plotting-javascript.qmd).
It is not part of the 216 static views.

```{=html}

```
 **Profile** selects reading or presentation text and mark sizes. **Surface** selects a
paper or panel background. The image keeps its chosen mode and surface even when this
website changes mode. Export the case that matches the destination. An embedded PNG or
SVG does not change theme automatically.

## Embed your chart

Copy the gallery source for your interface and run the displayed command, or
adapt the complete programs in the [Python](plotting-python.qmd),
[R](plotting-r.qmd) or [JavaScript](plotting-javascript.qmd) guide.
Use a qualitative palette for named categories, sequential for one ordered
magnitude, and diverging for change around a meaningful center. Keep the same
domain and limits when comparing charts across pages or slides.

Embed a reading export at its declared width. If your publishing system accepts SVG, use
it in place of PNG:

```markdown
![Category trends, magnitude and centered change](folio-light-reading-paper.png){width=640px}
```

A presentation case uses 1152 CSS pixels at its declared placement. Fit previews
are useful for comparing appearance, but shrink all text along with the image.
See [scientific choices and placement](plotting-packages.md) for the shared rules.

## View and download without JavaScript

[Open the complete static download index](_generated/plotting/index.html).
Every view has its PNG, sanitized report and runnable gallery source. Python
vectors are available for every case. The larger R vector collection is
represented by one configuration per family for both native R routes.
The selector shows exact availability, never an unexplained disabled download.

Python canvases are 8 × 8 inches, and R canvases are 8 × 9. Comparing them does not
claim pixel-identical native marker geometry or device quantization. Fit previews
change apparent text size. Use **intended** width (640 reading / 1152 presentation
CSS pixels) to inspect the declared placement. Narrow screens scroll without
cropping or inverting the image. [Python details](plotting-python.qmd) and
[R details](plotting-r.qmd).
